surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $43.6M, well above the preview's $37.5M estimate and its roughly $39M midpoint-pacing benchmark. Revenue also grew 31% year over year, with sequential growth accelerating sharply.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue grew 31% year-over-year to $43.6 million”; quarter-over-quarter growth accelerated from 6.7% in Q2 to 18.6% in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: revenue $37.5M”; the preview also identified “~$39M” as straight-line midpoint pacing and said the bull scenario was “≥$42M.”

surprises.description: BigBear.ai raised its full-year revenue guidance to $150–165M, lifting the floor by $15M and the midpoint by 5% rather than reaffirming the prior range. The range remained wide, but the higher floor was better than the preview's concern about another full-range affirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the first time to $150-165 million” and noted “a 5% increase versus prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior range was “$135M–$165M”; the preview said that “affirming the full wide range for a third straight quarter is itself a soft negative” and that buyers wanted “$145M+ floor language.”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share was much larger than the preview's estimate, but it was driven primarily by an unanticipated, noncash goodwill impairment. The impairment was $0.16 per share versus an expected loss of $0.05 per share, making the headline gap look substantially worse than the underlying operating result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss of $91.9 million ($0.19 per share)”; the loss was “driven primarily by a noncash goodwill impairment charge of $76.7 million ($0.16 per share).”

surprises.description: Gross margin improved year over year but fell short of the preview's expected range and its 32% watch threshold: it came in at 31.2%, not around 33% or higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 878 basis points year-over-year to 31.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “GM ~33%,” expected “GM 32–34%” in its base case, and listed “Gross margin ≥32%” as a catalyst checklist item.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was narrower than expected and improved from the prior quarter, contrary to the preview's concern that losses were worsening. It was still roughly flat year over year, so the improvement was not a year-over-year turnaround.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $9.1 million,” versus negative $9.4 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA of “$(11)M,” described a base case of “$(10)–$(12)M,” and said losses had widened to “$(11.6)M” in Q2.

surprises.description: Management emphasized a less capital-intensive strategy, whereas the preview had identified deploying cash into accretive M&A as an H2 priority and a possible catalyst. The call's emphasis was instead on the company's AI positioning and broader defense-AI investment tailwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management emphasized “a less capital-intensive strategy positioned in AI value-chain layers 4 and 5,” citing defense AI/autonomy budget requests and expected G7 investment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said commentary on deploying cash into “accretive M&A” was an H2 priority and called an M&A announcement a “live possibility.”

surprises.description: Cash and investments at quarter-end were nearly $400M, above the roughly $388M level implied by the preview's $409.8M June balance and its estimate of about $22M of quarterly cash burn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BigBear ended Q3 with nearly $400 million in cash and investments.”
